justification: Creates one new production table, cdc_lot_link, and commits the script that builds it. The table links each of the 181,750 complying-development certificates to the cadastral lot its coordinates fall inside, which is what turns 'what was approved at this address' into 'what was approved on lots like this one'. Nothing existing is modified: the build is purely additive and dropping the table reverses it completely. Also corrects DB_SCHEMA.md, whose header had been wrong by roughly half since February (58 tables against a real 118, 46,585 provisions against 55,696), and which omitted the four largest tables in the database entirely. The risk this report addresses is a silent wrong answer rather than a crash — a lot link that quietly fails, or a development type that quietly becomes NULL, both read as 'nothing there' rather than as an error.

pre_impl.existing_data: Four sweeps before writing. (1) git ls-files scripts/ matching cdc|certificate|lot_index|lot_join returned only validate_lot_index.py, a read-only drift harness comparing lot_search_index LEP values against the live MapServer — a different concern in the opposite direction. (2) grep for cdc_lot|certificates_by_lot|lots like this|comparable_approvals across services/ and frontend-nextjs/ returned zero. (3) information_schema showed complying_development_certificates (the source), cdc_eligibility_standards (CDC rules, not certificates) and lot_index_refresh_log (refresh logging) — no link table. (4) lot_search_index joins LOTS to PLANNING CONTROLS; this joins CERTIFICATES to LOTS. Different direction, different key, no overlap.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The pre-implementation protocol caught a real defect before a single row was written. development_type is jsonb, but stored in TWO shapes: 171,002 rows are a jsonb array and 10,748 (5.9%) are a jsonb STRING whose text is itself a JSON array — double-encoded. The obvious implementation guards with jsonb_typeof(...)='array' and lets the remainder fall through to NULL, which silently empties the 'what was built' field on 5.9% of the corpus, indistinguishable from a certificate that recorded no type. Decoding the string shape recovers all 10,748. Two other assumptions were checked and held: cadastre geom is SRID 4326 on every row with zero NULL geoms, so the ST_SetSRID(...,4326) literal needs no reprojection; and latitude/longitude are double precision with zero rows outside the NSW bounding box.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New table cdc_lot_link and new script scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py. No existing table, column or row is modified. DB_SCHEMA.md and the three architecture documents are edited to describe the new state. .gitignore gains one allowlist exception, because scripts/* is ignored by design with an explicit !scripts/<name> list — without the exception the build recipe for a live production table would have been silently untracked, which is the exact trap the comment block above that list warns about.

functions.name: BATCH_SQL — the point-in-polygon link plus development-type normalisation
functions.input: up to 2,000 certificates that have no row in cdc_lot_link yet, each with latitude, longitude and development_type
functions.output: one cdc_lot_link row per input certificate, carrying lotidstring, lot_area_m2, dev_types and a three-state match_status
functions.if_none: A certificate that matches no lot still gets a row, with match_status 'no_lot_at_point'. A certificate with no coordinates still gets a row, with 'no_coordinates'. Nothing is skipped, so an absent link can never be confused with an unattempted one — and this is also what makes the loop terminate.

functions.name: development_type shape normalisation
functions.file_line: scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py, the CASE jsonb_typeof block inside BATCH_SQL
functions.input: development_type, which is a jsonb array on 171,002 rows and a double-encoded jsonb string on 10,748
functions.output: a text[] of distinct development types, or an empty array where the source recorded none
functions.if_none: dev_types is NULL only when the shape is neither array nor string — a shape this script has never seen. Measured at build time: 0 undecodable, 36 explicitly empty, 181,714 with types. An empty array and NULL are deliberately different values, so 'the source said none' stays distinguishable from 'we could not read it'.

functions.name: report — the status readout
functions.input: the live cdc_lot_link table as it currently stands in production, read with no writes
functions.output: counts by match_status and by dev_types state, plus how many certificates remain unlinked
functions.if_none: If the table does not exist it says so rather than raising. If undecodable is non-zero it prints an explicit instruction to investigate, because that number being above zero means a storage shape has appeared that this script does not handle.

values.value: the 98.1% match rate and every count in the docs
values.read_at: the live database on 2026-08-10, immediately after the build, via scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py --status
values.if_missing: Every figure is reproducible by re-running that command, which is read-only. The counts are also recorded in docs/architecture/VERIFICATION.md beside the SQL that produces them. Certificates grew 181,737 to 181,750 between 08-09 and 08-10, so any count here is a measurement with a date, not a constant.

values.value: lot_area_m2, denormalised onto the link table
values.if_missing: NULL where the matched lot has no recorded area, and NULL for every non-matched row. It is a copy taken at link time, so if the cadastre is re-synced this column goes stale silently — that is the one field on this table with a staleness risk, and re-running the script does NOT refresh it for already-linked rows.

queries.query: SELECT ... FROM complying_development_certificates c0 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdc_lot_link k WHERE k.cdc_id = c0.id) LIMIT 2000
queries.purpose: Select only the certificates that have not been linked yet, so the build is resumable after an interruption and a no-op once complete. This is also the loop's termination condition.
queries.file_line: scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py, the inner subquery of BATCH_SQL
queries.where_clause: NOT EXISTS against the link table's primary key. Without it the script would reprocess the same first 2,000 rows forever. It is safe against non-matches specifically because a row is inserted for every certificate regardless of outcome — if non-matches were skipped instead, they would stay pending and the loop would never end.

queries.purpose: Find the cadastral lot a certificate's coordinates fall inside. This is the whole point of the table.
queries.file_line: scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py, the spatial LEFT JOIN LATERAL in BATCH_SQL
queries.where_clause: Guarded on latitude and longitude both being non-NULL, so the 25 coordinate-less certificates are classified rather than silently erroring. The 4326 literal was verified against the live catalog before writing — cadastre geom is SRID 4326 on every row, so no reprojection is needed and a mismatched-SRID silent miss is not possible. LIMIT 1 is a deliberate simplification for stacked strata parcels, documented in the module docstring: the linked lot is the parcel footprint, not the individual unit.

queries.query: CASE jsonb_typeof(development_type) WHEN 'array' THEN development_type WHEN 'string' THEN (development_type #>> '{}')::jsonb END
queries.purpose: Collapse the two storage shapes of development_type into one array before anything unnests it, so the 5.9% double-encoded rows are read rather than blanked.
queries.file_line: scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py, the dt_norm expression in BATCH_SQL
queries.where_clause: The CASE has no ELSE, so an unrecognised shape yields NULL rather than a wrong value — a loud gap instead of a quiet fabrication. Verified before writing that all 10,748 string-shaped rows decode to arrays, and confirmed after building that undecodable is 0.

break_it.scenario: The two storage shapes of development_type are not collapsed, so the 10,748 double-encoded rows get NULL dev_types
break_it.what_happens: Nearly 6% of certificates silently lose their 'what was built' field. Every downstream query filtering on development type under-reports, and because NULL reads as 'no type recorded' rather than as an error, nothing surfaces the loss.
break_it.how: Caught by the pre-implementation protocol before the first write, not after. The CASE handles both shapes, an empty array is stored distinctly from NULL, and report() prints the undecodable count on every run with an explicit instruction if it is above zero.
break_it.repro: SELECT jsonb_typeof(development_type), count(*) FROM complying_development_certificates GROUP BY 1 — 171,002 array against 10,748 string.

break_it.scenario: A certificate matches no lot and is skipped rather than recorded
break_it.what_happens: The 3,466 unmatched rows stay in the pending set forever, so the build loop never terminates. Worse, a later reader cannot tell 'we looked and found nothing' from 'we never looked'.
break_it.how: match_status is three-state and a row is written for every certificate whatever the outcome. That makes absence explicit and simultaneously guarantees the loop drains.
break_it.repro: SELECT match_status, count(*) FROM cdc_lot_link GROUP BY 1 — matched 178,259, no_lot_at_point 3,466, no_coordinates 25, summing to the full 181,750.

break_it.scenario: The geometry SRIDs do not match between the point literal and the cadastre
break_it.what_happens: Either every intersect raises, or worse it silently fails to find the cadastral lot under each point and the table fills with no_lot_at_point while looking like it ran correctly.
break_it.how: Checked before writing: SELECT DISTINCT ST_SRID(geom) FROM nsw_cadastre_lots returns 4326 only, with zero NULL geoms, matching the literal. A 98.1% match rate on the finished table is the confirming evidence — a silent SRID mismatch would have produced near-zero.

break_it.scenario: The build is interrupted partway and leaves the table half-populated
break_it.what_happens: A partial table that looks complete to any reader who does not check the count.
break_it.how: Each batch selects only unlinked certificates and inserts with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so re-running resumes exactly where it stopped. This was exercised for real: the first run was cut off at 50,000 rows and the second completed the remaining 131,750 with no duplicates and no gaps. --status reports how many remain.
break_it.repro: Interrupt the script, then run it again; then python scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py --status shows remaining 0.

break_it.scenario: lot_area_m2 goes stale after a cadastre re-sync
break_it.what_happens: Queries filtering on lot size use an area copied at link time, which may no longer match the cadastre. Wrong comparison set, no error.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated, and deliberately stated rather than hidden. Re-running the script links only NEW certificates; it does not refresh lot_area_m2 on rows already linked. Refreshing after a cadastre re-sync currently requires dropping and rebuilding the table, which takes about three minutes. This is the one staleness risk on this table and it is recorded in DB_SCHEMA.md and in the QA values section.
break_it.repro: Compare cdc_lot_link.lot_area_m2 against nsw_cadastre_lots.planlotarea for the same lotidstring after any cadastre sync.

post_merge.db_reset: None required. The build is additive: one new table, four new indexes, no change to any existing table, column or row. DROP TABLE cdc_lot_link reverses it entirely. The table is already populated in production as of 2026-08-10.
post_merge.secrets: None added. The script reads DATABASE_URL from the repository root .env, the same as every other script here. No credential appears in any committed file.
post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py --status should report 181,750 linked and 0 remaining, with undecodable at 0. Re-run it periodically — the certificate feed adds rows daily and the script links only the new ones, so it is safe as a scheduled job.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any SQL identifier written in code stops resolving against the live catalog — so if cdc_lot_link or any of its columns is dropped or renamed while code still references it, this exits non-zero. It passed after this change with no new invalid references (10 pre-existing defects remain suppressed by the baseline). Its honest limit: it checks that names resolve, not that the data behind them is right. The data-level invariant is that scripts/build_cdc_lot_link.py --status reports 0 undecodable and 0 remaining; that one reports rather than exiting non-zero, so it is a check a human reads, not a gate.
